summary.name: Dnote
summary.one_liner: Dnote is a free, open-source command line notebook for saving commands, snippets, and notes in the terminal, with full-text search and an optional self-hosted sync server.
use_cases: Saving useful shell commands for later reuse
Keeping code snippets searchable in the terminal
Taking notes without leaving the command line
Syncing notes across multiple machines with a self-hosted server
Building integrations with notes via a REST API
summary.what_it_does: Dnote is a terminal-based notebook for quickly capturing commands, snippets, and insights. It provides full-text search across all notes so commands can be found without scrolling shell history. Notes are stored in a single SQLite file that can be backed up, queried with standard tools, or migrated. It works with the user's own text editor, either inside a terminal or as a GUI. Optionally, it can run as a self-hosted server (single binary with SQLite, deployable via Docker or directly) that syncs data across devices and exposes a REST API.
notable: Single binary with no dependencies, stored in one SQLite file
Optional self-hosted sync server with REST API
Works with any text editor, terminal or GUI
caveats: Multi-device sync requires running the self-hosted server
